chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from al-Washshāʾ, from Abān, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, concerning the saying of Allah, the Exalted:
And know that whatever you gain from anything, then indeed one-fifth of it is for Allah, and for the Messenger, and for the near of kin.
He said: They are the relatives of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, and the khums is for Allah, and for the Messenger, and for us.

key_terms.الرَّسُولِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.خُمُسَهُ: its one-fifth share, the portion due as khums
key_terms.ذِي الْقُرْبَى: the near of kin mentioned in the verse
key_terms.غَنِمْتُمْ: you acquired or gained as spoils or gains
key_terms.قَرَابَةُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the relatives of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله

ai.seo_question: Who are “the near of kin” in the verse of khums, and who is entitled to khums according to Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Qur’anic phrase regarding khums by identifying “the near of kin” as the relatives of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله. It presents the verse as establishing the entitlement of Allah, the Messenger, and the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام to khums.

en.hubeali:
Al Hassan Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washha, from Aban, fromMuhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> regarding the Words of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Exalted
[8:41] And know that whatever war booty you gain, a fifth of it is for Allah and for the Rasool and for the near of kin.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They are the near of kin of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, and the fifth is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and for His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup> and for us<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Ibrahim ibn ‘Umar al-Yamani from Aban ibn abu ‘Ayyash from Sulaym ibn Qays who has said the following “I heard Amir al-Mu’minin Ali (a.s.) say, ‘We, By Allah, are the ones to whom Allah has referred by the words ‘Dhi al-Qurba’ (relatives) and has given the same status as to Him self and His the Holy Prophet (s.a).
He has said, “Whatever God grants to His Messenger (out of the property) of the people of the towns, belongs to God, the Messenger, the kinsfolk, the orphans, the destitute . .” [59:7]

It applies to such person from us exclusively. In the charity there no portion is appropriated to us. It is the way Allah has honored His Holy Prophet (s.a) and has honored us instead of feeding us the filthy things in the hands of people.”
